# atlassian_organization_policy (Resource)

Manages an Atlassian organization policy. Requires `read:policies:admin`, `write:policies:admin`, and `delete:policies:admin`.

> **Supported scope**
> Only `data-residency` policies without resource associations are supported for creation, import, and management. Use the organization policy data sources to read IP allowlists and other policy types.

A policy's type is specified by `data.attributes.type`; `data.type` is always `policy`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "atlassian_organization_policy" "example" {
  organization_id = "your-organization-id"

  data = {
    type = "policy"
    attributes = {
      type   = "data-residency"
      name   = "Japan data residency policy"
      status = "disabled"
      rule = {
        in = ["jp"]
      }
      # Only policies without resource associations are currently supported.
      resources = []
    }
  }
}
```

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = atlassian_organization_policy.example

  identity = {
    organization_id = "your-organization-id"
    policy_id       = "your-policy-id"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `organization_id` (String) Organization ID.
- `policy_id` (String) Policy ID.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = atlassian_organization_policy.example
  id = "organization-id,policy-id"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import atlassian_organization_policy.example 'organization-id,policy-id'
```
